existing_root_observation.interpretation: Each mechanism process consumed about one CPU core-equivalent in this phase; Census about 1.87. Cached seed303 had 19.779 GB logical read calls but only 130.589 MB physical reads. This supports repeated CPU/page-cache scanning rather than exclusively physical disk starvation; the sample does not isolate functions.

measured_bank_loading.interpretation: Hot cached requests remain approximately 0.993 s versus isolated SHA approximately 0.934 s on the representative bank. These are separate measured profiles, so this is supporting localization, not a measured percentage of current wall time or predicted speedup.

cache.capacity_evidence_limit: The one-tile profile has zero evictions. This audit did not read live whole-loop cache counters or establish full-working-set residency. Config history cites a 32-bank approximately 38 GB serialized working set, but serialized bytes differ from decoded resident size and this history is not a fresh capacity measurement.
cache.eviction_effect: CPU LRU eviction removes the decoded CPU bank and its GPU entries; next request reloads the original archive and rehashes. GPU-only eviction retains the CPU bank but requires a transfer. Full SHA occurs on every request independent of eviction.
cache.guard_semantics: Nested structural/storage/version metadata only, no copies, tensor reductions, or RNG.

narrow_successor_plan.capacity: Budget retained decoded CPU objects, any retained archive bytes, transient full archive decode, GPU copies and prefetch separately. Prefer a pinned complete active TRAIN/VAL working set within an explicit cap. If entries are evicted, their next verified acquisition still needs a cold read/hash/decode; do not claim once-per-worker verification for evicted bytes.
narrow_successor_plan.details: Read a bounded original archive byte snapshot once, verify those exact bytes against the registered bank SHA, and decode that verified snapshot with all original loader checks. Retain the exact returned fixed_prepared CPU object and original role/manifest/source/config bindings; use existing non-mutating storage/version guards on consumers. Hits return that retained decoded object rather than reopening or rehashing the live archive.
narrow_successor_plan.order: Keep current model-outer VAL and all training/serialization/scoring/checkpoint order for the first v2.
narrow_successor_plan.verification_semantics: The consumer must use the verified snapshot, never newly reopened unverified bytes. Keep binding identity drift failure, source/manifest full verification and original scientific checks. No SHA guard is silently disabled.

narrow_successor_plan.details: Prepare the next deterministic TRAIN or VAL bank on CPU while the current bank's GPU work runs, using the same snapshot provider, fixed float32 fields and original tile order. Bound prepared/raw/pinned buffers and surface preparation failures before consuming the tile.
narrow_successor_plan.limit: No current-worker patch, batch/mathematics/precision/RNG/selection changes or promised speedup.

narrow_successor_plan.RNG_and_dropouts: Original seal uses eval and no_grad. Source scans of the mechanism/age/anchor consumer modules found no forward random/dropout calls; seeding/shuffling occurs outside VAL. Thus reordering independent eval model calls can share a preparation, but exact logits/RNG/output/score parity remains part of root's qualification.
narrow_successor_plan.details: Process each original parent/tile bank once for all active eval-mode models and collect each model's logits at the original positions. Then serialize, seal, score and checkpoint in the original model-outer, parent order. Retain every model's tile order and exact CPU softmax/serializer.
narrow_successor_plan.recommendation: Separate from first v2 because verified decoded-bank hits already remove most repeated preparation while preserving all caller order.

narrow_successor_plan.limit: CPU accepted timing is not evidence of current CUDA throughput improvement.
